summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 1.1/64)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr məd ksiḥ u karmo, kəzze nošo, kmaləm ak karsəwone,
data.translation: Wenn der Weinberg geschnitten worden ist, geht jemand und sammelt die Rebzweige ein,

rationale: Introduces Detransitive Preterit; the following collection of branches establishes a completed pruning event.
Ksoḥo di ʕašire treats a human tribe as the patient of pruning. One clear nominal attestation, not a botanical participant extension.
ksiḥ u karmo is a completed patient-subject pruning event before collecting the cut branches. The previously empty Detransitive section gains one sense; only ksiḥ is attested here.

data.turoyo: [OJ: ṭaʕət mede, u mede d ṭaʕət, u ksoḥo das sate, aydarbo kkusḥile?]
data.translation: [O.J.: Du hast noch etwas vergessen – wie geht das mit dem Schneiden der Rebstöcke?].

rationale: Fills Infinitiv with the explicit patient construction das sate.

data.turoyo: [OJ: ṭaʕət mede, u mede d ṭaʕət, u ksoḥo das sate, aydarbo kkusḥile?]
data.translation: [O.J.: Du hast noch etwas vergessen – wie geht das mit dem Schneiden der Rebstöcke?].

rationale: Fills Infectum with the pruning question and singular patient suffix.

data.turoyo: Ar rawṭe, d howən qalləs w ab biži kokəsḥənne.
data.translation: Ranken, die schwächlich sind, und wilde triebe Schneidet man ebenfalls weg.

rationale: Adds plural patient resumption and contrasts weak shoots with wild growth.

data.turoyo: Walla kosaḥwayno bayn u karmo, hama lə ḥzeli. Xd u kalbo, mḥalaqla ruḥa l ṣawʕi, dwəṣlali.
data.translation: Ich beschnitt (Reben) im Weinberg, und ohne dass ich es sah, warf sie sich wie ein Hund auf meinen Daumen und biss mich.

rationale: Adds first-person Infectum-wa to the sparse box.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (MAC NE Interview 2/62)

data.turoyo: I. Bašqa dəmmina, ʕam u+ksoḥo, ʕam u+dworo?
data.translation: Anything else, let’s say, with the pruning, with the plowing?

rationale: Adds definite Infinitiv in an interview question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (MAC NE Interview 2/63)

data.translation: We didn’t go pruning (and) plowing, we wouldn’t sing.

data.turoyo: Bəṯr mu ksoḥo kodawrənne, kokərwənne. Naqqa komoḥən bi ʕaǧfo qm as sate.
data.translation: Nach dem beschneiden Ackert man die Wein Berge durch, d. h. man beackert sie zum ersten Male und lockert das Erdreich vor den Weinstöcken mit der Hacke auf.

rationale: Completes Infinitiv at five with the temporal sequence after pruning.

data.translation: Es bedeutet ja, daß der Stamm fast gänzlich ausgerottet wird.

rationale: Only attestation of the new figurative pruning-a-tribe subsense.

summary: All 16 occurrences were checked. Literal viticultural pruning remains sense 1 across vines, shoots and buds. The tribal pruning image warrants a figurative subsense, attested only in Infinitiv.

JTM 1.1/63 has generic plural agents, a singular shoot resumed by -le, plural vines resumed by -ne, nominal patient das sate, and possessed action noun ksoḥaṯṯe. Do not treat these argument-coding alternations as senses.

kosaḥwa and kosaḥwayno have root-initial k, not an additional k-indicative prefix. Infectum-wa backgrounds pruning when the bite occurs. ksiḥ is a completed Detransitive event with omitted agent, not an adjective chosen from the translation.
The same verse contains kasoḥo kayiso, a skilled pruner, which the occurrence list does not separately analyze. It is an agent designation; its productive status and box are not inferred here.
94/110's exact baseline clause, LuF 3/55 under LuF 302/55, and 115/5 are not re-added. The ʕam phrase in MAC NE Interview 2/62 concerns pruning in the interview and need not be strictly temporal.
Is kasoḥo in JTM 1.1/63 a lexical profession noun or a form the editors would index under Part act.?
Confirm the unattested partner of ksiḥ before supplying a full Detransitive base pair. The current proposal adds no reconstructed Infectum.

Does 29/92 imply literal mass killing or a threat to the tribe's continuity through the prohibited marriage? The metaphorical pruning/extermination sense is clear; its exact social consequence needs context beyond the supplied verse.
